hints: Focus on what the two Mr values are telling you, the jump from 84 to 164.9 must come from adding something across a reactive bond.
Calculate Mr for each skeleton using 12 for C, 1 for H and 16 for O, and remember HBr adds 80.9 in total.
Only an alkene with the right carbon count can both start at 84 and undergo electrophilic addition to reach 164.9, check which structure fits both tests.
walkthrough:
**Work out what the Mr change means**

Think simply first. HBr has an Mr of about 80.9, so 84 + 80.9 = 164.9.

$$M_r(\text{HBr}) = 1.0 + 79.9 = 80.9$$
This strongly suggests an addition reaction where the whole HBr molecule adds to an unsaturated compound.

**Calculate Mr of each starting compound**

Use $M_r$ rules with C = 12, H = 1, O = 16.

$$M_r(\text{A, cyclohexane, C}_6\text{H}_{12}) = (6 \times 12) + 12 = 84$$
$$M_r(\text{B, heptene, C}_7\text{H}_{14}) = (7 \times 12) + 14 = 98$$
$$M_r(\text{C, pentan-3-one, C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}) = 60 + 10 + 16 = 86$$
$$M_r(\text{D, hex-3-ene, C}_6\text{H}_{12}) = (6 \times 12) + 12 = 84$$
So only A and D start at 84.

**Test reactivity with HBr**

HBr reacts by electrophilic addition to a C=C double bond, but not with alkanes or ketones under these conditions.

$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{13}\text{Br}$$
Compound A is cyclohexane, an alkane with only single bonds, so no addition occurs. Compound D is hex-3-ene, an alkene, so it adds HBr to give $M_r = 84 + 80.9 = 164.9$. That is the match.

options.A: Cyclohexane, C6H12, does have Mr = 84, so it passes the first test. However it is a saturated alkane with no C=C bond, so it cannot undergo electrophilic addition with HBr. No bromoalkane product of Mr 164.9 is formed.
options.B: This is a C7 alkene (hept-3-ene, C7H14) so it would add HBr correctly, but its starting Mr is 98, not 84. Students choosing this spot the alkene reactivity but forget to check the carbon count carefully.
options.C: Pentan-3-one, C5H10O, has Mr = 86, not 84. It is also a ketone with a C=O group, not a C=C alkene, so it does not undergo addition with HBr in this way.
options.D: Hex-3-ene, C6H12, has Mr = (6 x 12) + 12 = 84. As an alkene it undergoes electrophilic addition of HBr to give C6H13Br with Mr = 84 + 80.9 = 164.9. It satisfies both conditions perfectly.
